plan.summary:
Webhook payloads are now normalized and signed with a real HMAC.

- `Event` trims whitespace from event names.
- `Sign` returns an HMAC of the body computed with the secret, using `hmacx.Sum`. Before, it hex-encoded the raw body, so the secret was not used.
plan.riskRationale: Signing is security-sensitive. The old code did not use the secret at all, so signatures were forgeable. Receivers that check old signatures will fail. The `Event` trim changes the output for names with surrounding whitespace.
plan.storyArc: The PR makes webhook output trustworthy. First the signing is fixed, since it is the security-critical change. Then event names are normalized so that they are consistent.

noise.reason: Only adds the hmacx import. The use of the import is in hunk-3, which stays in a topic.

topics.title: Sign webhook bodies with HMAC
topics.narrativeBrief: How does `Sign` change from hex-encoding the body to an HMAC keyed by the secret? Verify the `hmacx.Sum` semantics (hash algorithm and argument order) in the source, and the effect on receivers that verify signatures.

topics.title: Trim whitespace in event names
topics.narrativeBrief: What does `Event` now return for names with leading or trailing whitespace? Check the callers to see whether the trimmed name feeds the signed payload.
